chunks: Ali ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) while he was saying to his servants: 'Do not slaughter until the dawn rises, for Allah has made the night a tranquility for everything.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, but what if we fear?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you fear death, then slaughter.'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a phrase of respect)

ai.seo_question: When is the best time to slaughter an animal according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) derives the ruling from the divine wisdom that night is designated as a period of tranquility (sakan) for all creatures, thereby establishing the general prohibition of slaughter during darkness. The hadith provides a practical exception for cases of necessity, such as fear of death or spoilage, illustrating the Shia juristic principle of balancing general tranquility with specific exigencies. This narration is foundational in al-Kafi for understanding the temporal boundaries of ritual slaughter within the broader Islamic emphasis on mercy and order in creation.
